household-demand-leisure: $I\in\{H,W\}$ indexes the husband/father and wife/mother. $w_I$ is the market wage in dollars per hour. $\theta_I$ is the dimensionless productive share of a childcare hour; $\theta_Iw_I$ is its productive shadow price and $(1-\theta_I)w_I$ its process-benefit price.

$I\in\{H,W\}$ indexes the spouses. $Y$ is full expenditure and $Y_R=Y-e_T-e_M$ remaining full expenditure, in dollars/week. $w_H,w_W$ are wages in dollars/hour and $L_I$ full leisure in hours/week. $F_I$ is the full-leisure demand and $F_I^{-1}$ its local inverse in remaining expenditure. $e_T$ and $e_M$ are weekly time and monetary child costs.

$I\in\{H,W\}$ indexes spouses. $w_I^*=\theta_Iw_I$ is the productive shadow wage in dollars/hour; $e_T$ is weekly time cost. $\alpha^*,\beta_I^*,\gamma_I,\gamma_{WH}$ are cost-function coefficients. $H,W$ index father and mother. $t_H,t_W$ are care hours/week, $w_I$ wages in dollars/hour, and $\theta_I$ dimensionless productive shares estimated freely. $m^*$ is latent purchased care and $m$ observed care expenditure in dollars/week. $\alpha,\beta_I,\gamma_I,\gamma_{WH}$ are coefficients. $z^{T,I},z^T$ contain a constant, spouses’ ages and education, child number and an indicator for a child under three. $(u,v_W,v_H)$ are jointly normal, mean-zero disturbances with unrestricted covariance. $I\in\{H,W\}$ indexes spouses. $L_I=l_I+(1-\hat{\theta}_I)t_I$ is full leisure in hours/week; a hat denotes an estimate. $w_H,w_W$ are hourly wages and $Y_R=Y-e_T-e_M$ remaining full expenditure (rescaled to thousands of dollars in estimation). $a_I,b_I,c_I,d_I,e_I$ are demand coefficients; the coefficient $e_I$ is distinct from child cost. $z^{L,I}$ contains a constant, spouses’ ages and education. $\varepsilon_I$ has zero mean and unrestricted covariance across spouses.

$I\in\{H,W\}$ indexes spouses. $L_I$ is full leisure in hours/week, $w_I$ the hourly wage, $Y$ full expenditure, and $Y_R=Y-e_T-e_M$ its remaining part. children-costs-one-adult-household: $\omega$ is the adult clothing budget share, $\varphi$ the adult’s dimensionless resource share and $1-\varphi$ the children’s share. $y$ is nondurable expenditure in 1987 pounds/week, $p$ the relative clothing-price index and $\pi$ the dimensionless Barten price scale. $g$ is the childless adult’s clothing-demand function.

$\omega$ is the adult clothing budget share; $p$ is the relative clothing-price index and $y$ nondurable expenditure in 1987 pounds/week. $z^\omega$ contains a constant, education, age and its square, participation, ownership, decades and region. $\alpha,\beta,\gamma,\eta$ are demand coefficients and $\epsilon$ the residual. Systems are estimated separately for women and men.

$i\in\{f,m\}$ indexes women and men. $\varphi_i$ is the adult resource share and $\psi_i$ its logistic index. $y_i$ is expenditure in 1987 pounds/week and $p_i$ the relative clothing-price index. $z_i^\varphi$ contains sharing-rule covariates, excluding decade indicators. $\boldsymbol n_i$ is the vector of child characteristics, $n$ the number of children and $\widetilde n$ the remaining child characteristics in the alternative specification. $\theta_z,\theta_y,\theta_p,\theta_n$ are index coefficients; $\rho$ is the alternative family-size exponent. A prime denotes transposition.

$i\in\{f,m\}$ indexes women and men. $\pi_i$ is the dimensionless Barten scale, $y_i$ expenditure in 1987 pounds/week, $p$ the relative clothing-price index, $n_i$ the number of children and $\kappa_i$ the scale coefficient.

$i\in\{f,m\}$ indexes women and men. $\omega_i$ is clothing’s budget share, $p_i$ relative clothing price, $y_i$ weekly expenditure in 1987 pounds, $\varphi_i$ the adult resource share and $\pi_i$ the Barten scale. $z_i^\omega$ contains a constant, education, age and its square, participation, ownership, decades and region. $\alpha_i,\beta_i,\gamma_i,\eta_i$ are coefficients and $\epsilon_i$ the residual. $D_i=1$ for a parent and zero otherwise; $A_i$ is the nonlinear parent adjustment displayed in the second line.
